notes.ente: The same word for one and many.
notes.envubu: Plural: viboko, but animals agree like people: kiboko mkubwa.
notes.mkali: Also “strict” for a person: mwalimu mkali. Many: wakali.
notes.hatari: Never changes its form: Ni hatari! (It’s dangerous!)
notes.wengi: For people and animals: watu wengi, ndege wengi.

guidebook.intro: From the goat in the yard to the elephants of the Serengeti, animals are everywhere in Swahili life, and in its proverbs.

tips.title: Animals agree like people
body: Most animal names look like n- nouns and don’t change in the plural: **mbwa** is one dog or many. But the words that describe them agree as if they were people: **simba mkali** (a fierce lion), **mbwa wangu** (my dog), **tembo wawili** (two elephants), **ndege wengi** (many birds).
Where an animal is uses **yuko**, like a person: **Paka yuko jikoni**. For many animals, **wako**: **Nyani wako juu ya mti**.

culture.title: Safari is a Swahili word
body: **Safari** simply means “journey” in Swahili. It came into English through hunting and tourism in East Africa, along with **simba**, **rafiki** and **hakuna matata**.

culture.title: Cows and wealth
body: Among many East African communities, cattle are wealth and part of marriage gifts. Asking **Una ng’ombe wangapi?** (how many cows do you have?) can be a serious question.
